title: V. General canons 1–6 on the divine attributes
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): V. But here general CANONS are to be observed. 1. Ye attributes belonging toward God, or His essential properties, [many] in one manner are, because ye whole infinite perfection belonging toward ye divine essence in one concept we cannot comprehend, but only to some extent apprehend. 2. In ye attributes belonging toward God prior plus posterior there is not except as regards us. For since all with ye essence one are, in themselves prior plus posterior they do not admit. 3. Ye attributes belonging toward God more plus less in themselves do not admit. But their effects intensification plus remission can admit. 4. Ye attributes belonging toward God unto one another contrary are not. But their effects contrary can be, as ye sun by one plus ye same virtue mud hardens plus wax melts. 5. Ye attributes belonging toward GOD in themselves viewed altogether incommunicable are. For God's very essence itself they are. Yet into communicable plus incommunicable not wrongly are they distinguished, because some their image upon creatures impress, as wisdom plus goodness, some scarcely a vestige or thinnest shadow. 6. Ye attributes belonging toward God in ye persons belonging toward ye Holy Trinity are not multiplied. For just as one essence belonging toward Father, Son, plus Holy Spirit there is, so also one eternity, omnipotence, etc. there is. Therefore although ye Father omnipotent is, plus ye Son omnipotent, plus ye Holy Spirit omnipotent: yet three omnipotent ones there are not, but those three one omnipotent GOD are.
pass_b_english: V. But here general CANONS are to be observed. 1. The attributes of God, or His essential properties, [are many] in one manner, because we cannot comprehend the whole infinite perfection of the divine essence in one concept, but only apprehend it to some extent.

2. In the attributes of God there is not prior and posterior except as regards us. For since all are one with the essence, in themselves they do not admit prior and posterior. 3. The attributes of God do not admit more and less in themselves. But their effects can admit intensification and remission. 4. The attributes of God are not contrary to one another. But their effects can be contrary, as the sun by one and the same virtue hardens mud and melts wax.

5. The attributes of GOD viewed in themselves are altogether incommunicable. For they are God's very essence itself. Yet they are not wrongly distinguished into communicable and incommunicable, because some impress their image on creatures, as wisdom and goodness, some scarcely a vestige or thinnest shadow. 6. The attributes of God are not multiplied in the persons of the Holy Trinity. For just as there is one essence of Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, so also there is one eternity, omnipotence, etc. Therefore although the Father is omnipotent, and the Son omnipotent, and the Holy Spirit omnipotent: yet there are not three omnipotent ones, but those three are one omnipotent GOD.
source_text: V. Sunt autem hic observandi generales CANONES. 1. Attributa Dei, sive proprietates ipsius essentiales, uno modo, quia infinitam essentiae divinae perfectionem uno conceptu totam comprehendere nequimus, sed aliquatenus duntaxat apprehendimus. 2. In attributis Dei non est prius & posterius nisi quantum ad nos. Quia enim omnia cum essentia unum sunt, in seipsis prius & posterius non admittunt. 3. Attributa Dei non recipiunt magis & minus in seipsis. At effecta eorum possunt admittere intensionem ac remissionem. 4. Attributa Dei non sunt sibi invicem contraria. At effecta eorum possunt esse contraria, ut sol una eademque virtute sua indurat lutum & liquefacit ceram. 5. Attributa DEI in se spectata sunt prorsus incommunicabilia. Sunt enim ipsissima Dei essentia. Neque tamen perperam distinguuntur in communicabilia & incommunicabilia, quia quaedam creaturis imprimunt sui imaginem, ut sapientia, bonitas, quaedam vix vestigium aut umbram tenuissimam. 6. Attributa Dei non multiplicantur in personis S. Trinitatis. Sicut enim una est essentia Patris, Filii & Spiritus sancti: sic quoque est una aeternitas, omnipotentia &c. Quapropter licet Pater sit omnipotens, & Filius omnipotens & Spiritus s. omnipotens: tamen non sunt tres omnipotentes, sed tres illi sunt unus omnipotens DEUS.
